resources.string: allow-lan
Control whether proxy ports serve only this machine or accept connections from other LAN devices.
Enable it when phones, tablets, or other LAN devices must use this computer as a proxy.
This only changes a candidate override. Opening a LAN listener also requires suitable binding, authentication and access restrictions.
authentication
Defines username and password pairs for HTTP, SOCKS, and Mixed inbounds.
Use it when serving other devices on a network that is not fully trusted.
Previews and exports contain these credentials in plain text. Do not share the complete document.
disable-keep-alive
Disables keep-alive on mihomo outbound TCP connections.
Enable it only after identifying keep-alive as the compatibility problem.
Long-lived connections may be reclaimed more easily by NAT or firewalls, so this is rarely a good default.
dns.cache-algorithm
Selects LRU or ARC eviction for the DNS cache.
Choose based on whether domain access is stable or frequently changing.
It affects eviction only and does not change upstream correctness or TTLs.
dns.default-nameserver
Provide bootstrap DNS for DoH, DoT, and other upstream hostnames to avoid resolver startup dependencies.
It is required when nameserver entries use hostnames rather than IP literals.
Prefer directly reachable IP resolvers and do not depend on an upstream that itself needs bootstrapping.
dns.direct-nameserver
Lists dedicated upstreams for destinations routed DIRECT.
Use it for regional split DNS or LAN names that must resolve directly.
The follow-policy option determines whether nameserver-policy is also used. Keep resolvers reachable independently.
dns.direct-nameserver-follow-policy
Apply nameserver-policy when resolving direct destinations.
Use existing domain-specific DNS choices for direct traffic too.
Policy matches can change the selected resolver; check policies for local domains.
dns.enable
Enable mihomo DNS so answers can participate in rule matching and Fake-IP handling.
Enable it for TUN, transparent proxying, or centralized DNS policy.
Fake-IP, DNS hijacking, and related features do not work correctly when it is disabled.
dns.enhanced-mode
Choose redir-host or fake-ip to return real addresses or virtual addresses used for domain mapping.
TUN commonly uses fake-ip, while compatibility-sensitive setups may use redir-host.
Switching changes cache and connection semantics; related state may need to be reset.
dns.fake-ip-filter
Configure domain filters so LAN, device discovery, and other services incompatible with Fake-IP can receive suitable answers.
Add entries when virtual addresses break login, discovery, or certificates.
Real answers can change routing behavior and DNS-leak boundaries.
dns.fake-ip-range
Sets the CIDR used to allocate Fake-IP addresses.
Adjust it to avoid LAN or enterprise network conflicts while fake-ip is enabled.
It must not overlap real routes, and changing it invalidates old mappings.
dns.fake-ip-range6
Sets the IPv6 prefix used to allocate Fake-IP addresses.
Use it when dns.ipv6 and fake-ip are both enabled and clients genuinely need IPv6 Fake-IP.
The default may interact with browser local-network protections; dns.ipv6 stays off by default, and custom values require TUN route verification.
dns.fallback
Lists alternate upstreams used when primary DNS answers need fallback.
Use it for cross-region resolution or occasional primary-resolver failures.
fallback-filter decides when answers are used, and too many upstreams increase query cost.
dns.fallback-filter
Defines when a primary DNS answer is rejected in favor of fallback.
Configure it for pollution resistance or region-dependent answers.
Broad conditions send nearly everything to fallback; narrow ones may fail to correct bad answers.
dns.ipv6
Allow IPv6 answers from the mihomo DNS resolver.
Enable when applications need AAAA results on an IPv6-capable network.
Check IPv6 routing and Fake IP settings together. This does not change the Android system resolver.
dns.ipv6-timeout
Sets how long DNS waits for IPv6 results.
Adjust it when IPv6 is intermittently unavailable or slower than IPv4.
Too short drops usable IPv6 answers; too long adds connection startup delay.
dns.listen
Sets the address and port of the mihomo DNS listener.
Configure it when the host or LAN devices should use Jeemi DNS.
A non-loopback binding exposes a DNS service and must not become an open resolver.
dns.nameserver
Lists the primary upstream resolvers for ordinary DNS queries.
Configure supported UDP, TCP, DoT, DoH, or DHCP resolvers here.
Order and protocol affect latency, privacy, and availability; avoid duplicate or conflicting local additions.
dns.nameserver-policy
Selects specific DNS upstreams by domain, rule set, or geosite condition.
Use it when LAN, regional, or service-specific domains require different resolvers.
Keys and resolver formats must be valid; broad matches can shadow the default nameserver.
dns.prefer-h3
Allows DoH upstreams to prefer HTTP/3.
Enable it on networks with reliable UDP/443 and an H3-capable resolver.
Restricted networks may block QUIC; disable it when DNS becomes slow or unreliable.
dns.proxy-server-nameserver
Resolve proxy server domains separately to avoid depending on a proxy connection that is not established yet.
Configure it when subscription node servers are hostnames and normal DNS uses a proxy.
Use a trusted resolver reachable before any proxy starts, or all hostname-based nodes may fail.
dns.proxy-server-nameserver-policy
Choose DNS upstreams by proxy server domain to avoid resolution failures or dependency loops.
Use it with a non-empty proxy-server-nameserver when selected node domains require specialized resolution.
These policies require a non-empty proxy-server-nameserver. Home emits this override only when it is enabled.
dns.respect-rules
Routes DNS queries according to the active routing rules.
Use it for split DNS or resolvers that require different egress policies.
Bad dependencies can create DNS-routing loops; proxy-server-nameserver must also be correct.
dns.use-hosts
Controls whether mihomo DNS reads hosts entries from the configuration.
Use it for LAN aliases, test domains, or fixed-answer overrides.
An incorrect hosts entry directly breaks the affected destination.
dns.use-system-hosts
Controls whether mihomo DNS reads the operating-system hosts file.
Enable it when enterprise or development tooling already manages system hosts.
Other software can modify that file; inspect it while diagnosing unexpected answers.
etag-support
Let providers check updates using HTTP ETag to avoid downloading unchanged files again.
Enable it when rule and proxy providers support ETag and bandwidth matters.
Broken servers can return stale cache decisions; temporarily disable it while diagnosing missed updates.
experimental
Contains mihomo features that are still marked experimental.
Use an option only when current official documentation explicitly calls for it and rollback is available.
Fields may change or disappear between core releases; review them before every mihomo upgrade.
global-ua
Sets the global User-Agent used by mihomo to download subscriptions and providers.
Use it when a provider requires a specific User-Agent or requests should be standardized.
Some services return different content by User-Agent; verify results after changing it.
hosts
Defines static IPs, aliases, or fixed answers for domains.
Use it for LAN hosts, development, fixed services, or temporary corrections.
Static records do not track real service changes and a wrong value makes the domain unreachable.
interface-name
Selects the default system interface used for outbound dials.
Use it with Ethernet, Wi-Fi, VPN, or multiple routing uplinks.
Interface names are platform-specific and can change; an invalid value can break every outbound connection.
ipv6
Allow mihomo to resolve and connect to IPv6 destinations.
Enable when the device and upstream network support IPv6.
DNS IPv6 results have a separate switch. An unreachable IPv6 path can delay connections.
keep-alive-idle
Sets how long a TCP connection stays idle before keep-alive probing begins.
Adjust it on mobile networks or NATs that reclaim idle sessions quickly.
Too short adds needless probes; too long delays detection of dead connections.
keep-alive-interval
Set the TCP keep-alive probe interval to maintain idle connections and detect failed sessions.
Adjust it when network devices aggressively remove idle sessions.
Very short intervals add traffic and wakeups; evaluate it together with keep-alive-idle.
lan-allowed-ips
Lists client IPs or CIDRs allowed to reach proxy inbounds.
Use it when only selected home or office devices may use the proxy.
Overly broad CIDRs admit unintended clients; review interaction with the deny list.
lan-disallowed-ips
Lists client IPs or CIDRs denied access to proxy inbounds.
Use it to block guest, container, or untrusted networks.
DHCP can change addresses; do not accidentally deny the host or its management network.
listeners
Defines additional mihomo inbound listeners and their protocols, addresses, and ports.
Use it for supported inbound protocols such as Shadowsocks, VMess, or TUIC.
Names and ports must be unique; public bindings require authentication and exposure review.
log-level
Choose the minimum level of messages emitted by mihomo.
Adjust the amount of detail when diagnosing a core issue.
Silent disables core logs and hides Logs from the More menu. Other levels expose the log page; debug logs can contain connection details. Restart an active session to apply a saved level.
mixed-port
Accepts HTTP and SOCKS proxy connections on one port.
Use one local proxy port for applications that support HTTP or SOCKS.
Use a free port from 1 to 65535. Saving the value does not start a listener.
ntp
Configures mihomo network-time server, port, and update interval.
Use it when certificates or handshakes fail because the device clock drifts.
NTP uses UDP and requires a trusted reachable server; it does not replace full operating-system time management.
profile
Configures persistence of selector choices, Fake-IP mappings, and related mihomo state.
Use it when selections and Fake-IP state should survive mihomo restarts.
Persistent files must stay under jeemi_data; disabling storage changes post-restart behavior.
proxy-providers
Defines proxy-node providers that mihomo can load and refresh.
Use it when a subscription already uses providers or an additional managed node source is required.
URLs, paths, and health checks can be sensitive; this remains advanced YAML and is validated in the real final configuration.
redir-port
Set the Linux REDIRECT transparent proxy port receiving TCP traffic redirected by firewall rules.
Use it when Linux iptables REDIRECT is explicitly managed outside Jeemi.
A port alone does not install firewall redirection. Android VPN routing requires a separate service integration.
routing-mark
Set Linux routing marks on mihomo outbound connections for policy routing and avoiding transparent proxy loops.
Use it in advanced Linux transparent-routing setups.
This depends on privileged Linux routing facilities. Ordinary Android VPN permissions do not provide that access.
skip-auth-prefixes
Lists source networks that may bypass inbound username/password checks.
Use it when an automation cannot authenticate and its source address is stable and trusted.
A broad CIDR bypasses authentication; revisit exemptions when LAN addressing changes.
sniffer.enable
Enable domain sniffing.
Use this field in a local resource associated with subscriptions needing different domain detection.
Applying edits the draft only. Save and start or restart VPN to use the changes. Domain sniffing cannot read encrypted content.

sub-rules
Defines named ordered rule blocks invoked by SUB-RULE entries.
Use it when multiple entry rules should share one matching sequence.
Names must be unique and referenced correctly; cycles or missing terminal behavior can fail.
tcp-concurrent
Try multiple IPs returned by DNS concurrently to reduce TCP connection delays from an unreachable address.
Enable it for dual-stack or multi-address targets with inconsistent paths.
It creates short bursts of parallel dials and may not suit resource-constrained or concurrency-sensitive environments.
tls
Provides certificate and private-key settings for the mihomo external controller.
Use it only when controller TLS is required and certificates are managed deliberately.
Certificates and private keys may be sensitive. Adding this mapping does not create a controller or TLS listener.
tproxy-port
Set the Linux TPROXY transparent proxy port receiving TCP/UDP traffic with original destinations preserved.
Use it only with matching Linux policy routes and TPROXY rules.
This requires privileged routing and firewall rules. Saving a port does not provide Android VPN support.
tun.auto-redirect
Uses supported platform redirection features to optimize TUN capture.
Enable it only where the operating system explicitly supports it.

It requires platform networking capabilities and privileges and can cause loss of connectivity when unsupported. Android support depends on the future VPN adapter; this field alone cannot configure device routing.
tun.dns-hijack
Lists destinations whose DNS traffic is intercepted by mihomo DNS.
Use it to capture UDP or TCP port 53 in TUN mode.
Broad interception can break local DNS services, and DoH or DoT is not captured automatically. Android support depends on the future VPN adapter; this field alone cannot configure device routing.
tun.endpoint-independent-nat
Enable endpoint-independent NAT for TUN UDP to improve reachability for some P2P, gaming, and real-time communication traffic.
Use it when stable UDP mappings are required and default behavior is incompatible.
It changes UDP mapping and security behavior and should not be enabled without a specific need. Android support depends on the future VPN adapter; this field alone cannot configure device routing.
tun.exclude-interface
Excludes traffic originating from selected system interfaces.
Use it in multi-VPN, virtual-machine, or container networking setups.
Excluding the real default uplink can disable proxy connectivity; verify every interface. Android support depends on the future VPN adapter; this field alone cannot configure device routing.
tun.gso
Enable TUN Generic Segmentation Offload (GSO) to reduce packet processing during large transfers.
Enable it only after the platform and driver are known to support GSO.
Compatibility varies; disable it first when packet loss or corruption appears. Android support depends on the future VPN adapter; this field alone cannot configure device routing.
tun.gso-max-size
Limits the maximum aggregated segment size when TUN GSO is active.
Tune it only after tun.gso is enabled and platform profiling justifies it.
It has no effect without GSO and oversized values can break transfers. Android support depends on the future VPN adapter; this field alone cannot configure device routing.
tun.include-interface
Captures traffic only from selected system interfaces.
Use it to proxy only Wi-Fi, Ethernet, or one virtual interface.
Interface names are platform-specific and may conflict with exclude-interface. Android support depends on the future VPN adapter; this field alone cannot configure device routing.
tun.mtu
Set the maximum transmission unit of the TUN interface.
Adjust it while diagnosing fragmentation, partial page loads, or nested VPNs.
Too large causes fragmentation or loss; too small reduces efficiency. Android support depends on the future VPN adapter; this field alone cannot configure device routing.
tun.route-address
Lists destination CIDRs that should receive TUN routes.
Use it for partial routing or custom split-tunnel ranges.
Overlaps and split default routes can create loops or break LAN access. Android support depends on the future VPN adapter; this field alone cannot configure device routing.
tun.route-address-set
References rule sets whose address ranges should enter TUN.
Use it when route ranges are maintained by an ipcidr provider.
The referenced rule set must exist and be compatible with IP address sets. Android support depends on the future VPN adapter; this field alone cannot configure device routing.
tun.route-exclude-address-set
References rule sets whose address ranges must bypass TUN.
Use it when private or enterprise networks are held in an ipcidr provider.

Missing or stale providers change the routing boundary, so validate the final configuration before startup. Android support depends on the future VPN adapter; this field alone cannot configure device routing.
tun.strict-route
Installs stricter routing to reduce traffic bypassing TUN.
Enable it when leak prevention matters and platform compatibility has been tested.
It can affect multi-interface, virtualization, and LAN access; verify all of them. Android support depends on the future VPN adapter; this field alone cannot configure device routing.
tun.udp-timeout
Sets how long an idle TUN UDP session is retained.
Increase it when games or voice applications lose sparse UDP sessions.
Too short interrupts sessions; too long keeps large amounts of dead state. Android support depends on the future VPN adapter; this field alone cannot configure device routing.
tunnels
Defines port-forwarding tunnels created by mihomo.
Use it for services reachable only through the proxy or local port mappings.
Listener ports must be unique; public bindings expose services, and targets and policies must exist.
unified-delay
Use consistent connection timing for node tests to reduce differences caused by protocol handshakes.
Enable it for fairer comparisons across different proxy protocols.
Results still depend on the test URL, caches, and current network and do not represent throughput.
